papers.title_en: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
papers.authors: Sergey Salishev, Zeev Volkovich, Oleg Granichin
papers.evidence: 面向通用硬件算子的Transformer编译
papers.tldr: Transformer常被视为需专用算子和量化流程的模型，限制其在通用神经网络与硬件上的统一部署。论文证明含注意力、LayerNorm和GELU MLP的Transformer块可精确编译为固定仿射、路由及若干基础非线性组成的通用网络。理论指出，若去除激活值间乘法，稠密注意力每头至少额外需要N²次标量非线性；保留逐元素乘法即可避免该代价。针对稀疏注意力，提出尾部质量估计与聚类选键，在多模型上等价复现并优于直接丢弃尾部，为通用NPU执行和标准后训练量化提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. Without activation-activation products, every transform-wise compilation adds at least $N^2$ scalar nonlinear evaluations per head for dense scores. Keeping that one operation type removes this cost; its elementwise form, present on every surveyed NPU, suffices with the sigmoid and inverse square root. For top-$k$ attention with exchangeable tail scores, we prove that exact or conditional-mean tail mass gives an unbiased, minimum-mean-square-error estimate of the attention distribution, while tail drop is conditionally biased. When queries or agents cluster, centroids choose the keys first, reducing the number of computed scores from $N^2$ to $Nk$ per head. On DeiT-Tiny, MambaIRv2-Light and Pythia-70M the compiled models match their references with all keys, standard post-training quantization applies, and the exact tail-mass estimate beats tail dropping with half as many keys on DeiT-Tiny and, for $k\le8$, on Pythia-70M.

papers.title_en: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning
papers.authors: Junyu Lin, Bosong Qi, Pengcheng Shi, Jiayuan Li
papers.evidence: 异构客户端条件下的个性化联邦学习
papers.tldr: 个性化联邦学习中的高本地准确率，可能掩盖客户端罕见或未见类别上的识别失败，也难以反映最差客户端的服务质量。论文提出FedGRC：以共识引导表征学习和多层度量合成构建共享统计空间，再按本地样本支持度收缩类别均值实现个性化。在3个数据集、5种异质性设置下对比21种方法，CIFAR上全局识别和个性化下限至少提升2.17%与2.13%。工作同时给出覆盖本地、全局、罕见、未见类及最差客户端的评测协议，为兼顾泛化与公平个性化提供方案。
papers.abstract_en: Real-world deployment of personalized federated learning (PFL) requires adapting to heterogeneous clients while preserving recognition performance beyond local distributions. However, high local accuracy can conceal failures on locally rare or absent classes. Effective personalization should therefore strengthen global recognition while raising the personalization floor. We propose an evaluation protocol that complements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations to reveal generalization obscured by local scores, and assesses personalization floors among the worst-performing clients to expose weaknesses hidden by aggregate performance. To meet these deployment challenges, we propose FedGRC, a unified PFL framework integrating generalization and personalization through (i) Consensus-Guided Representation Learning (CGRL), which learns discriminative representations through shared directional and magnitude guidance; (ii) Multilayer Metric Synthesis (MMS), which constructs a shared covariance metric from these multilayer representations for statistical classification; and (iii) Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization (SASP), which adapts class means within this metric by shrinking local estimates toward shared means according to local sample support, enabling adaptation while retaining shared knowledge. Extensive experiments, including benchmarking against 21 methods across 5 heterogeneity settings on 3 datasets and comprehensive ablation studies, validate the effectiveness of FedGRC. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, FedGRC surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines in global recognition and personalization floors by at least 2.17% and 2.13%, respectively. On the real-world heterogeneous FedRS dataset, it outperforms the respective best baselines by 2.15%, 3.30%, and 4.61% in local adaptation, global recognition, and the personalization floor.

papers.title_en: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
papers.authors: Tianzhe Chu, Druv Pai, Yi Ma
papers.evidence: 面向可扩展预训练的条件计算架构
papers.tldr: 大规模模型常用MoE通过稀疏激活专家降低计算，但条件计算主要局限于前馈层。论文提出Nestor，在注意力算子中引入另一种条件稀疏，并与MoE稀疏形成层级嵌套。在相同计算量和稀疏度下，Nestor语言预训练优于常规MoE；持续预训练中更易扩展长上下文、适应新领域且遗忘更少。结果表明，替代性条件计算机制可提升模型规模化训练与持续学习能力。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. In MoE transformers, this sparsity arises in the MoE operator, which generalizes the multi-layer perceptron in the classical transformer. In this work, we explore an alternative mechanism for conditional computation that analogously generalizes the attention operator. The sparsity induced by this mechanism naturally nests (i.e., hierarchically composes) with the sparsity induced by the MoE operator. We show that a transformer employing this nested sparsity mechanism, which we call Nestor, performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining. We also show that Nestor is well-suited for continual pretraining: it can be adapted to longer contexts more effectively than conventional MoEs, as well as adapt more efficiently to new domains while forgetting less on old domains. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits persist as model size, dataset size, and context length grow. Our results demonstrate the potential of alternative conditional computation mechanisms for deep neural network architectures. Code and checkpoints are available on GitHub at https://github.com/Ma-Lab-Berkeley/Nestor .

papers.title_en: Measuring the Energy Cost of Completing Tasks with Quantized Language-Model Agents
papers.authors: Stephen Abkin, Aldric Yang, Alex Flesher, Nitheesh Kodarapu, Deepak Panigrahy, Aakash Tyagi, David Kebo Houngninou
papers.evidence: 量化大模型智能体的任务级能耗评测
papers.tldr: 量化通常按单个输出词元衡量节能，但智能体完成编码、数据分析等任务需反复调用模型、工具与修订，低精度还会改变成功率和生成量。论文在29个可自动验收任务上，对两种开源模型的4位与8位版本测量词元级及任务级CPU、GPU能耗。结果显示4位普遍降低每词元能耗，却可能因额外生成词元使单个完成任务的耗能最高增至3.5倍。研究提出以完成任务所需词元数结合词元节省评估精度，为本地智能体部署提供决策依据。
papers.abstract_en: Quantization reduces the memory and energy needed to serve large language models (LLMs) and AI agents for coding and data analysis can now run on locally hosted LLMs. In practice, this benefit is commonly benchmarked per output token. Yet an agent calls its model repeatedly, runs tools, and revises its work, and quantization can change both how much the agent generates and whether it succeeds. Existing energy studies either compare quantized models on single requests or measure agents at one fixed precision, overlooking how a change in precision plays out across a complete agent task.   To address this gap, this paper presents the first characterization of the task-level energy trade-offs of model quantization in locally hosted agents. We develop 29 agent tasks with automatic pass/fail checks in six families, ranging from single-answer SQL analytics to multi-step repository bug fixing, and measure CPU and GPU energy per output token and per completed task for 4-bit and 8-bit versions of two open-weight models on bare-metal NVIDIA A100 nodes with llama$.$cpp.   Our findings reveal that 4-bit precision generally saves energy per token, though whether it saves energy per completed task is task dependent and changes with the model and the execution budget (i.e., limits on turns, tokens, and time). We trace this discrepancy to the extra tokens needed to complete a task in full, which translates into using up to 3.5 times as much energy per completed task. These findings offer actionable guidance for developers and operators choosing model precision for agents, showing how tokens per completed task, set against the per-token saving, reveal whether lower precision completes the work with less energy.

papers.title_en: SPARE: Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy for Efficient MoEs
papers.authors: Yifan Yang, Hanling Yi, Dongquan Yang, Feng Lin, Rong Xiao, Aijun Li, Xiaotian Yu
papers.evidence: 面向部署的内存高效混合专家稀疏分配
papers.tldr: MoE虽能以较低计算成本扩展参数规模，但专家权重带来显著显存与部署负担，现有剪枝通常对各层平均分配稀疏率。SPARE利用校准数据上的路由熵，衡量Top-K门控权重是否分散，并据此为不同层分配不同剪枝量。它无需训练、与专家选择器无关，在相同预算下显著优于均匀剪枝。该工作将路由不确定性转化为可解释的层级稀疏分配信号，尤其提升高剪枝率下的性能保持能力。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale model capacity efficiently, yet their substantial memory footprint poses a major barrier to deployment. Expert pruning reduces this footprint, but most methods focus on which experts to remove and prune every layer equally. We propose SPARE (Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy), a training-free, selector-agnostic method that decides how many experts to remove from each layer using routing entropy, the entropy of tokens' normalized Top-K gate weights on calibration data. When a token's gate weight is spread evenly, removing one active expert discards little of it, so SPARE prunes layers with more diffuse routing more aggressively. A perturbation bound under random pruning formalizes this intuition, and controlled interventions with a fixed selector link concentrated routing to larger output changes. With the same selector and budget, SPARE improves average accuracy over uniform allocation on Mixtral, Qwen3, and DeepSeek models, especially at high pruning ratios. At 50% expert pruning, it raises the eight-task average of Qwen3-30B-A3B from 57.2% to 63.8%, and the math, code, and science average of DeepSeek-R1 from 80.1 to 82.8.

papers.title_en: WaRP: Workload-Aware Request Planning for Vector Retrieval on Object Storage
papers.authors: Ruipeng Wan, Xinyu Zeng, Yiming Qiao, Huanchen Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向向量检索基础设施的对象存储优化
papers.tldr: 现代向量检索常将向量载荷置于对象存储，逐簇读取会受固定请求延迟和按请求计费制约，而固定阈值合并策略难适配不同数据与负载。WaRP将探测簇的字节区间分组建模为全局查询优化，结合并发能力、请求上限，以动态规划和自适应前沿搜索生成近最优合并方案。其离线重排进一步提升区间可合并性且不改变检索语义。在AWS S3七个数据集上，WaRP加重排将QPS提升1.09—3.48倍、GET数降低2.12—5.19倍，并保持原有召回率。
papers.abstract_en: Modern vector search systems keep payload vectors in cloud object storage and only a compact routing index on fast local storage, typically using cluster-based ANN indexes. This design inherits a problem existing systems do not address. On object storage, small Range-GETs have latency dominated by fixed per-request overhead and are billed per request. Existing readers either issue one request per probed cluster, or coalesce adjacent ranges with hand-tuned gap or span thresholds that do not transfer across datasets or query workloads.   We formulate the grouping of probed-cluster byte intervals into object-store requests as a global per-query optimization problem and present WaRP, a workload-aware request planner that solves it efficiently. Given the sorted byte intervals, a limit on the number of requests per query, and an estimate of how many object-store requests from one query can proceed concurrently under the target serving configuration, WaRP searches for a merge plan that minimizes a concurrency-aware latency surrogate while satisfying the request limit. Using an optimized dynamic program and adaptive frontier search, WaRP returns a plan within $(1{+}ε)$ of the optimum, with per-query planning overhead under $10$ms even in the most demanding tested settings. A lightweight offline reordering pass further improves request mergeability without changing the semantics of ANN search.   We implement WaRP inside Lance's I/O scheduler and evaluate it on AWS S3. We build IVFPQ indexes on seven datasets, including SIFT100M and DEEP100M at the 100M-vector scale. WaRP + Reorder improves QPS by $1.09--3.48\times$ and reduces GETs by $2.12--5.19\times$ relative to Lance, while preserving Lance's recall.

papers.title_en: Spike-Aware Gradient-Based Mixed-Precision Quantization of Spiking Neural Networks for Vision Applications
papers.authors: Rajshekhar Rakshit, Devgokul B., Rakshitha Kalkura, Gopalakrishnan Srinivasan
papers.evidence: 面向高效神经网络部署的混合精度优化
papers.tldr: 脉冲神经网络依赖事件驱动与稀疏计算，适合低功耗视觉推理，但低比特量化易造成精度损失；现有基于Hessian的混合精度方案还需跨时间步展开，内存和计算开销较大。本文以一阶梯度评估层敏感度，提出脉冲感知的自适应位宽分配，避免二阶Hessian计算。在ImageNet的ResNet-34上，4.78倍压缩下达到73.30%准确率，同时较HAWQ-V2节省2.31倍内存、加速100倍位宽分配。该方法推动混合精度SNN在视觉任务中的高效部署。
papers.abstract_en: In recent years, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have gained massive attention as an energy-efficient neural computing paradigm due to their event-driven and sparse computing capability. However, maintaining accuracy under low-precision constraints, necessary for practical deployment, has been largely unexplored for SNN models. In addition, existing Hessian-based approaches for quantization, such as HAWQ-V2, incur significant memory and computational overhead due to temporal unrolling across multiple SNN timesteps. We propose a spike-aware gradient-based mixed-precision quantization framework for SNNs that adaptively assigns bit-widths using first-order gradient information, avoiding costly second-order Hessian computations. We evaluate our method across various SNN-based architectures, including VGG, ResNet, and Vision Transformer models obtained from both ANN-to-SNN conversion and direct training frameworks, on CIFAR10/100, ImageNet, and DVS-CIFAR-10 datasets. Notably, on ResNet-34 evaluated on ImageNet, our method achieves 73.30% accuracy at 4.78$\times$ compression, which is comparable to that provided by HAWQ-V2, while reducing memory consumption by 2.31$\times$ and bit-allocation runtime by 100$\times$. We also present an energy analysis for mixed-precision SNNs showing that the proposed quantization strategy enables energy-efficient deployment without compromising performance.
